_comment: Expected TDX boot-chain measurements for the OS images the 0G-PC gateway is
deployed on. `pcverify -gateway` embeds this file, so nobody running it has to
supply or even know these values.
WHAT IT IS FOR. The quote's mr_config_id commits to a compose hash, but the host
chooses that register — what makes it truthful is the guest OS refusing to boot
when it disagrees with the app-compose actually delivered (dstack
config_id_verifier.rs). Trusting that check means trusting the OS doing it, and
MRTD + RTMR0-2 are what identify it. Without an entry here, a host that booted a
MODIFIED dstack OS with that check removed could commit to a published release's
compose hash while running something else, and verification would still pass.
AN ENTRY IS (IMAGE, VM SHAPE), NOT AN IMAGE. MRTD and RTMR0-2 are a function of
the image AND the VM it booted on — vCPU count, RAM size, PCI topology, GPU
count. dstack deliberately does not publish per-image MR tables for this reason
(see the TdxOsImageMeasurement docs in dstack-types). Record the vm_config each
entry was computed for; an entry that names only an image version is wrong.
HOW TO DERIVE ONE. Do not copy values out of a running deployment: that only
records what it currently reports, which is the thing being verified. Recompute
them from the image's reproducible build, then confirm they match a live quote:
cargo build --release -p dstack-mr-cli   # from github.com/Dstack-TEE/dstack
dstack-mr diagnose --vm-config vm-config.json --image-dir <image> \
--actual-mrtd <hex> --actual-rtmr0 <hex> --actual-rtmr1 <hex> --actual-rtmr2 <hex>
vm-config.json is the vm_config the CVM reports; --image-dir needs the image's
ovmf.fd / bzImage / initramfs.cpio.gz / metadata.json. A clean diagnose plus a
match against the live quote is what makes an entry trustworthy — the computation
is independent of the deployment, and the comparison shows they agree.
An empty `images` list means NOT CONFIGURED: pcverify reports the OS image as
unpinned and says so in its summary, rather than failing. It never means
'accept anything' — see attest.BootChainPolicy.
